article_content: Research by the Australian Psychological Society has concluded that women are more prone to mental health problems attributed to stress from societal pressures. The 2014 survey marked a year with higher stress levels for women, as well as greater impact on overall wellbeing compared to men. Professor Lyn Littlefield of APS pointed out the damage stress can do to mental and physical health, and the importance of addressing its root causes. Financial and familial concerns were identified as major stress factors among women, with over half of women indicating these as the primary sources of their stress. The study revealed that women experience a stronger impact of stress on their health than men, with percentages for physical and mental health issues being higher for women. Interestingly, those over the age of 66 reported greater levels of wellbeing. The findings, which underscore the well-being gap between genders, were released to coincide with National Psychology Week, suggesting the need for societal conversations on managing stress.

article_content: Tom Horne, Arizona's Attorney General, has put forth a proposal to arm one principal or other designated school official in the event of school attacks, as a supplementary measure to existing safety protocols. The situation is made complex by budgetary restrictions reducing the presence of school resource officers. Horne's plan would see one individual fully trained to handle situations involving firearms, equipped to secure a weapon at the school while maintaining the ability to promptly alert authorities in emergencies. The argument behind this proposal cites the post-9/11 FAA pilot arming initiative and fuses financial and security considerations – a preventative better than doing nothing after a tragedy such as Sandy Hook. Arizona's sheriffs have shown support for the proposal, with legislative action anticipated. The plan, as detailed by Horne, seeks a middle ground between the potential dangers of more teachers needing to carry firearms and inaction in the face of future school crises.

El argumento para esta propuesta incluye el programa de armas para los pilotos después de los atentados del 11 de septiembre del FAA, combinando consideraciones financieras y de seguridad - prevenir mejor que no planear nada tras una tragedia como Sandy Hook. Los sheriffs de Arizona han expresado respaldo para la propuesta, con el líder de la fracción republicana estatal anunciando la participación legislativa.
